When a Supabase project is **paused** on the free plan it’s only the **billing state** that changes, not the data itself. | What happens when paused | What you can still do | What you cannot do | |--------------------------|-----------------------|--------------------| | The plan is put into a “read‑only” state | • You can view and query the database (with the same SQL or your client)
• You can download a CSV, export the schema, or copy tables to another project
• You can check the settings page | • No new rows can be written, updated or deleted
• No new uploads to the storage bucket
• No new users can sign‑up or log in (auth is still listed but no writes) | So your data is **not gone**. It’s just frozen until you **resume** the project. ### How to resume 1. Log in to the Supabase dashboard. 2. On the left side, click **“Billing & plan”**. 3. You’ll see a button that says **“Resume project”**. Click it. 4. Confirm the action. After that, the free plan is active again, writes return, and you can keep using the project normally. ### If you’re worried about data loss - **Take an export**: In the Database section, you can export each table to CSV/SQL just in case. - **Backup the project**: Under “Settings → Backups”, you can trigger a backup, then download it and store it locally or in another storage bucket. If you’ve had the project paused for a while, the data remains, but the free tier may have some limits on how long it keeps a paused project (usually a few months of inactivity before it’s deleted automatically). If that’s a concern, resume it as soon as possible or copy your data to a new project.
